newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani police detain 200 people in murder case.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani police detain 200 people in murder case.

text.p: Pakistani police said on Sunday they had detained more than 200 people for questioning about the killing of the head of Karachi's power utility.

Police said they had also agreed to register a case against unidentified activists of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) on a complaint of Shahnaz Hamid who accused MQM of being behind the murder of her husband Shahid Hamid.

Hamid, 46, managing director of the state-owned Karachi Electric Supply Corporation was shot dead, along with his driver and guard, in an attack by four gunmen in the affluent Defence Housing Society of Karachi on Saturday.
Hamid had served as Sindh provincial home secretary from March 1995 to February 1996, a period that coincided with a crackdown against MQM militants in Karachi.
An MQM spokesman denied any involvement in Hamid's killing and said the party might issue a detailed statement later.
Newspapers on Sunday quoted Farooq Sattar, an MQM leader and senior minister in the Sindh provincial government of which MQM is a coalition partner, as saying the murder was a conspiracy.
"Shahid Hamid's murder is part of an organised conspiracy aimed at weakening the Sindh government and to provide grounds for action against the MQM," Sattar was quoted as saying.
A senior police official said more than 200 people including some political activists had been detained for questioning but gave no details.
More than 150 people have been killed in political violence in the southern port city in the past four months, compared to over 500 in 1995 and more than 2,000 in 1996.
